entry.title: Defensive Programming Rule #3: Validate Your Enums (Every Time)
entry.summary: Enums enhance code readability but can lead to errors if not validated, as any integer can be cast as an Enum, including invalid values. Validating Enum inputs prevents silent data corruption, ensures meaningful defaults, and avoids processing impossible states. Always validate at method boundaries and define a zero value as "unknown."

entry.title: SQL Server Myth: “Checkpoint Only Writes Pages from Committed Transactions”
entry.summary: Checkpoints in SQL Server are often misunderstood. Contrary to popular belief, they don’t only flush committed data they write all dirty pages, even from uncommitted transactions. Transactional safety comes from the log and recovery process, not from checkpoint filtering.

entry.summary: Parameter validation is crucial in programming, ensuring applications reject bad data before it causes issues. Consistent validation fosters reliable APIs.
